quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In risk management and personal safety at home, school, or camp, what is the difference between a hazard and a risk, and why must both smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms be maintained?
quiz_item.question: In risk management and personal safety at home, school, or camp, what is the difference between a hazard and a risk, and why must both smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms be maintained?
options: A. A hazard and a risk mean the exact same thing, and smoke detectors automatically detect odorless carbon monoxide gas without a separate CO sensor.

B. A hazard is an unsafe condition or source of potential harm, while risk is the likelihood and severity of injury from that hazard; smoke alarms detect fire early while CO alarms detect colorless, odorless carbon monoxide from fuel-burning appliances.
C. A hazard only exists outdoors during camping trips, and carbon monoxide alarms should be installed inside attic vents rather than near sleeping areas.
D. Risk can be eliminated only by avoiding all physical activity, and smoke alarm batteries only need testing once every ten years.

requirements.req_text: Family and Home Safety. Do the following: (a) Explain common causes of and prevention of home injuries. (b) Discuss the dangers involved with the use of fireworks. (c) Explain common causes of and prevention of home fires. (d) Using the Home Safety Checklist in the Safety merit badge pamphlet, or one approved by your counselor, inspect your home or a similar building for hazards with an adult. Review your checklist and findings with your counselor. (e) Develop a fire-escape plan for your home or for a similar building. Include in your drawings exit routes from each room and a meeting place outside. Conduct a fire-escape drill. Review your plan and your drill with your counselor. (f) Develop a family emergency action plan for evacuation because of weather or other natural disasters that occur in your area. Outdoor Family Meeting Place: As part of the drill, family members should gather at the meeting place outside the home, as specified in the family plan (p. 51).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Gather at Outdoor Meeting: As part of the drill, family members should gather at the meeting place outside the home, as specified in the family plan (p. 51).
Step 2 - Use Bedding for Escape: If time allows, bedding can be used in an emergency to aid an escape (by tying sheets together to make a rope) or cushion a fall (p. 51).

Step 3 - Guard Personal Information Online: Never give outpersonal information to anyone you meet online or without your parent or guardian's permission (p. 18).
Step 4 - Prevent Identity Theft Risks: Identity theft is the fastest-growing crime in the United States (p. 18).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: In risk management and personal safety at home, school, or camp, what is the difference between a hazard and a risk, and why must both smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms be maintained?
options: A. A hazard and a risk mean the exact same thing, and smoke detectors automatically detect odorless carbon monoxide gas without a separate CO sensor.

B. A hazard is an unsafe condition or source of potential harm, while risk is the likelihood and severity of injury from that hazard; smoke alarms detect fire early while CO alarms detect colorless, odorless carbon monoxide from fuel-burning appliances.
C. A hazard only exists outdoors during camping trips, and carbon monoxide alarms should be installed inside attic vents rather than near sleeping areas.
D. Risk can be eliminated only by avoiding all physical activity, and smoke alarm batteries only need testing once every ten years.
choices: A. A hazard and a risk mean the exact same thing, and smoke detectors automatically detect odorless carbon monoxide gas without a separate CO sensor.

B. A hazard is an unsafe condition or source of potential harm, while risk is the likelihood and severity of injury from that hazard; smoke alarms detect fire early while CO alarms detect colorless, odorless carbon monoxide from fuel-burning appliances.
C. A hazard only exists outdoors during camping trips, and carbon monoxide alarms should be installed inside attic vents rather than near sleeping areas.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. A hazard is an unsafe condition or source of potential harm, while risk is the likelihood and severity of injury from that hazard; smoke alarms detect fire early while CO alarms detect colorless, odorless carbon monoxide from fuel-burning appliances.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Identifying hazards allows you to reduce risk before an accident happens, and installing working smoke and CO alarms on every level and near sleeping areas protects against both fire and invisible carbon monoxide poisoning.
